# dsh-editor-context
> **English · 中文**

Turn the lines you are looking at in Cursor / VS Code into a chip in the DSH
composer.

Type `@`, pick **editor position**, and a chip lands in your draft. Send it, and
the model receives
the file and the range:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That is the whole feature. The position reaches the conversation because you put
it in your own sent

ence — nothing is injected behind you — so there is no
numbering to disambiguate, no auto-injection

to switch off, and nothing to
configure. A reference you typed needs none of that.
## What you need

- DSH 0.2.x, running the web profile (`dsh web`) — verified on `0.2.2-alpha.2`
- The editor half: **

Editor Context**, `pandarayc.editor-context-bridge` on the
Marketplace,
0.5.0 or newer. It publishes

`~/.editor-context/windows/*.json` and announces
the WebSocket this plugin dials in `~/.editor-cont

ext/windows/*.json` and announces
the WebSocket this plugin dials in `~/.editor-context/endpoints/`.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package is not on npm yet, so `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-editor-context`
does not resolve
; use the repository form above until it does.
## Use

In the composer, type `@`. An **editor position** group appears with one row —
where you are right n

the composer, type `@`. An **editor position** group appears with one row —
where you are right now:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Picking it puts a chip in your draft as a word in your sentence. Type around it,
edit it, delete it,

never send it: it is ordinary draft text, and it stays a chip
in replayed history too.

The chip is short (`limit.go:146-154`), but the model receives the full token.
The send path expands

every reference through its owner's codec before it goes
out, so the model sees an address it can o

through its owner's codec before it goes
out, so the model sees an address it can open, not a label.
| You insert | The model receives |

| `@<absolute path>#L146` | the caret is on line 146 |
| `@<absolute path>#L146-L154` | lines 146-15

th>#L146` | the caret is on line 146 |
| `@<absolute path>#L146-L154` | lines 146-154 are selected |

**The absolute path is what the model gets**, because `relativePath` in the state
file is relative t

o the *editor's* workspace root, which is generally not the
agent's working directory — `read` could

's* workspace root, which is generally not the
agent's working directory — `read` could not open it.

**Why `#L`.** DSH's shipped file rule treats everything after `@` up to
whitespace as a path, so `@p

ath:12-34` would have the colon swallowed into the
path and two rules claiming the same span. `#` is

outside that grammar, so this
token's ownership is unambiguous — and `#L` is the line-address spell

ing models
already know from web forges.
## From the editor, without switching windows

The same position can be sent from Cursor / VS Code instead of typed here:
**Add to Bot** on the edi

tor title bar. The chip appears in your draft the moment
you click, so you can point at three places

in a row and then ask one question
about all three.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The extension runs the WebSocket **server** and this plugin is the **client**.
That direction is not

arbitrary: Node ships a WebSocket client and no server, so
the half that needs a library is the one

living in a VSIX — which is why this
plugin still has no dependencies at all.

One extension window is one server, and a port only one process can hold, so the
extension announces

where each window actually ended up in
`~/.editor-context/endpoints/<pid>.json`. The plugin reads t

hat directory and
keeps **one link per window** — a second window, a restarted extension or a
change

d port all look the same from here: the next scan sees a different
directory than the last one. `wsU

rl` is still dialled when the registry is empty,
which is what a pre-0.5 extension looks like.

Neither hop is an interval. The editor pushes; the plugin's long poll parks until
there is something

to hand the browser. An idle conversation is one open socket
and one parked response, not a request

browser. An idle conversation is one open socket
and one parked response, not a request per second.

The delivery carries the **text** as well as the address and the range. A delivery
is a snapshot, no

t a pointer: a pointer goes stale the moment the file is edited,
moved or reverted, and the agent is

then reasoning about code that no longer
exists.
## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`wsUrl` is the **fallback**, not the address: with extension 0.5.0 or newer the
real endpoint comes

from the registry, and this is only dialled when the registry
is empty. If the extension sets a toke

n, this side needs the same string or the
publisher refuses the subscription — and a refusal is term

inal, reported once,
because a wrong secret is still wrong thirty seconds later.

The plugin mounts a read-only `GET /editor-context/position` on DSH's web server,
which the browser

half reads. It returns an address and a line range — never file
contents. A path the extension's `ex

cludeGlobs` rejected answers 404, so the
exclusion rule does not leak the path it is hiding.
### `/editors`

Typing `/editors` in a conversation opens a picker of the **editor windows this
plugin is talking to

** — app name, project folder, state and pid. Picking one
inserts *that* window's current position i

nto the draft, which is the DSH-side
equivalent of going back to the editor and pressing Add to Bot.

It is a picker rather than a status dump because the question behind it is
"which Cursor am I pointi

ng at", and with two windows open that has no single
answer. It is named `editors` and not `status`:

`status` describes a whole
process, and a keyword nobody can guess is a failure of its own.

The same data is on `GET /editor-context/editors`, one entry per link with its
state (`absent`, `con

necting`, `ready`, `refused`), dial count, and the `hello`
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- **A path containing spaces needs the quoted form**, `@"a b.go"#L12`. The rule
parses it; the candi

date list does not yet produce it.
- **Clicking a chip does not jump back to the editor.** The exten

sion only writes
files and has no inbound channel.
- **Exclusion is configured on the extension side

**, not here. The plugin has no
rules of its own, and none are needed: it can only offer what the ex

tension
chose to publish.
